I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—since the winter quiet settled in, really. Out at the ranger station, it’s just me most days, and the silence gets loud. I don’t know when it started, but sometimes in the evenings, after my patrol, I end up eating… a lot. More than I should. A whole package of pasta, maybe some canned meat, bread, dessert—just keep going even after I’m full. I don’t plan it, but the kitchen’s there, and the loneliness feels heavier once the sun’s down.

I’ve started eating in the back room, not the common area, just so no one sees. Not that there’s anyone around. Used to share meals with folks during shift changes, but now I wait till they leave. It’s not every day, maybe two or three times a week? But when it happens, I don’t stop till my stomach aches.

I’m not sad all the time, but some mornings I can’t find a reason to start the coffee. I sleep okay, mostly. Just… feel hollow sometimes. Not like before my wife passed, not that deep grief—but like a shadow’s moved in. I can’t tell if I’m slipping or just getting old.
D023-D013_h001.question_a:
I’ve been feeling low since my wife passed two years ago—just a constant loneliness that won’t lift. Lately, I’ve been eating these huge meals by myself, even when I’m not hungry. Like, I’ll go through half a package of ground beef in one chili, plus bread, chips, the whole thing—more than anyone should eat in one sitting, let alone a man my age. And I keep eating until I’m truly uncomfortable, sometimes to the point I can’t button my field pants.  

I don’t do this with anyone around. It’s always after work, once I’m back at the cabin. I’d be embarrassed for someone to see—what would they think? A grown man shoveling food like he’s trying to fill a hole? It happens most evenings, been going on for about four months now.  

I feel down a lot, sure—I miss her terribly, don’t get out much anymore. But I still go to work, care for the trails, check in with rangers. I just don’t feel joy in things like I once did. Still, I wouldn’t say I’m hopeless or worthless—just… tired. Sad, but not broken.
D023-D013_h001.question_b:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about the past four months, ever since my wife passed. Out in the woods, I used to find peace—now it just feels empty. I’m not sleeping well, if at all. Most days I can’t get out of bed until noon, and even small tasks like fixing a meal feel overwhelming. I don’t enjoy anything anymore—no watching the birds, no tending the garden. I just sit.  

I’ve started eating a lot—way more than I used to. Some evenings, I’ll open can after can, eat straight from the pan, even when I’m painfully full. I don’t know why I keep going. It’s shameful, so I do it alone after dark. I know it’s not normal, but I feel numb while I’m doing it, and at least then I don’t feel the ache in my chest.  

I feel useless, like my life doesn’t matter now. Sometimes I think my family would be better off without me. This sadness isn’t just grief—it’s heavy, constant, and it’s taken over everything. The overeating is a problem, sure, but it’s like it’s just one part of this deeper darkness I can’t climb out of.
